The complete guide to what a MEME actually is! 🧠

📖 DEFINITION:
The word 'meme' was coined by biologist Richard Dawkins in his 1976 book 'The Selfish Gene'. He used it to describe a unit of cultural information that spreads from person to person — like a cultural gene.

On the internet, a meme became:
A piece of humorous or relatable content that spreads rapidly across the web, often remixed, modified, and adapted by thousands of people.

📅 HISTORY OF INTERNET MEMES:

🔹 1996 — 'Dancing Baby' (Baby Cha-Cha): One of the first viral internet clips
🔹 1999 — 'All Your Base' text meme from a Japanese game
🔹 2001 — 'Hamster Dance' — viral audio + animation
🔹 2005 — LOLcats / 'I Can Has Cheezburger' — image macros explode
🔹 2007 — Rickrolling — clicking links that lead to Rick Astley's Never Gonna Give You Up
🔹 2009 — Rage Comics — stick figure comics expressing emotions
🔹 2010 — Troll Face / 'Challenge Accepted' / Advice Animals
🔹 2011 — Nyan Cat, Planking, Rebecca Black's Friday
🔹 2012 — Gangnam Style, YOLO, Honey Badger Don't Care
🔹 2013 — Doge ('much wow such meme'), Harlem Shake
🔹 2014 — Ice Bucket Challenge, 'But That's None Of My Business'
🔹 2015 — Dress Colour debate (Blue/Black or White/Gold), Whip/Nae Nae
🔹 2016 — Harambe, Salt Bae, Pen Pineapple Apple Pen, Arthur's Fist
🔹 2017 — 'This Is Fine' dog, Distracted Boyfriend, Blinking White Guy
🔹 2018 — 'Is This A Pigeon?', Moth Lamp, Two Buttons, Drake Pointing
🔹 2019 — Baby Yoda (Grogu), 'OK Boomer', Area 51 raid
🔹 2020 — Pandemic memes, Bernie Sanders mittens, WAP
🔹 2021 — NPC memes, Grimace Shake, 'Nobody Asked'
🔹 2022 — 'Girl Dinner', AI memes, 'It's Giving'
🔹 2023 — 'Rizz', 'Slay', AI-generated meme formats
🔹 2024-2025 — Brainrot, Italian Brainrot (Bombardino Coccodrillo), Sigma memes, 'Delulu'

Memes are now: communication, emotion, identity, memory, social currency. That's why Dezzme exists. 🔥

What makes a GREAT meme? 🏆

The science of viral memes:

1️⃣ RELATABILITY
'omg that's literally me' = VIRAL
The wider the audience who identifies with it, the faster it spreads.

2️⃣ TIMING
A meme referencing a current event spreads faster than a timeless one. That's why 'seasonal' memes exist.

3️⃣ ADAPTABILITY (Memetic fitness)
The best memes become TEMPLATES. Distracted Boyfriend works for hundreds of situations. Drake Pointing works for any comparison.

4️⃣ SIMPLICITY
Great memes communicate in seconds. Complicated = doesn't spread.

5️⃣ EMOTIONAL RESONANCE
Funny, sad, angry, surprised — the emotion hits fast and hard.

6️⃣ SHARED CONTEXT
In-group humor ('you had to be there') creates community around the meme.

Meme formats that always work:
• Before/After comparisons
• 'Me when...' scenarios
• Expectation vs Reality
• Character A vs Character B
• Increasing absurdity (escalation)
• Breaking the 4th wall

Examples: Italian Brainrot, Skibidi Toilet, Gyatt content

🐕 DOGE (2013)
Origin: Photo of a Shiba Inu dog with Comic Sans text in broken English ('much wow', 'so amaze', 'very doge'). Became one of the most enduring meme formats ever. Also inspired the Dogecoin cryptocurrency! 'Much wow, such coin.'

Origin: Screenshot from Drake's 'Hotline Bling' music video. Top panel = Drake looking disapproving. Bottom = Drake looking pleased. Used for any 'prefer this over that' situation.

Origin: Bait-and-switch prank where a link claims to be something else but leads to Rick Astley's 'Never Gonna Give You Up'. Still works in 2025. 'You got Rickrolled!'

Internet Culture — the full guide! 🌐

🗣️ INTERNET SLANG DICTIONARY:

📌 COPYPASTA — A block of text copied and pasted everywhere, often absurdly long or threatening. The Navy Seal Copypasta ('What the f*** did you just f***ing say about me...') is the most famous example. On Dezzme, copypastas go in the text feed!

😈 TROLLING — Deliberately provoking people online for entertainment. Ranges from harmless jokes to serious harassment.

💩 SHITPOSTING — Deliberately low-effort, ironic, or absurd content posted for laughs. Quality doesn't matter — vibe does. Gen Z elevated this to an art form.

👾 CURSED CONTENT — Images/videos that feel deeply wrong, unsettling, or uncanny but in an amusing way. 'That's cursed' = something shouldn't exist but does.

🌟 GOING VIRAL — Content that spreads exponentially. Something 'goes viral' when shares/reposts create a feedback loop of exposure. No formula guarantees it.

💜 STAN CULTURE — Extremely devoted fandoms, usually around music artists or celebrities. Named after Eminem's 2000 song 'Stan' about an obsessive fan.

❌ CANCEL CULTURE — Mass collective criticism of a public figure for perceived bad behavior. Can range from genuine accountability to mob mentality.

😂 GEN Z HUMOR EXPLAINED:
• Absurdist — Random, nonsensical, out of context
• Self-aware — Meta humor about humor itself
• Anti-humor — Deliberately 'unfunny' as the joke
• Irony stacking — So many layers of irony meaning is lost
• NPC content — Treating people as background characters

Why Gen Z humor confuses older generations:
It's often intentionally BAD. The badness IS the joke. Traditional humor = setup + punchline. Gen Z humor = subvert expectations so hard there is no punchline. That IS the punchline.
